## What the turning points share

- **Each new answer was framed against death or the corpse.** Breath is what the dead lack
  [[6]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-tertullian-to-breathe-is-to-live). Heat is what the corpse has lost
  [[19]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-longitudine-to-live-is-to-be-warm-and-moist). Descartes's dead body is a clock run down
  [[44]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-descartes-death-body-decays-not-soul-leaves), Bichat's life is what resists death
  [[77]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-bichat-1800-ensemble-des-fonctions), and Huxley's living matter dies continually
  [[81]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-huxley-1868-continual-death).
- **A turn changes where life is placed more often than what it is.** In the body's heat
  [[18]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#wil-aristotle-life-is-maintenance-of-heat), in a giver [[27]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-nicene-spirit-zoopoion-vivificantem), in the
  world [[52]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-absurd-that-world-not-live), in organisation [[75]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#wil-kant-organism-formative-power-not-machine),
  in a feeling [[109]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#mod-wilmans-aliveness-childhood-1898).
- **Each new definition came with a new practice.** The lamp brought regimen and the hope of a long life
  [[35]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-arnald-old-age-can-be-retarded). The living cosmos brought the art of drawing in the world's spirit
  [[50]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-world-animated-spirit-applied). The felt quality brought exercises for the hands
  [[112]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#mod-ramacharaka-hands-aliveness-1906). (Idea 3 follows these practices.)
- **The losing side keeps writing.** The living world was contested in antiquity
  [[57]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-anc-living-world-was-contested), survived the machine in Conway and Cavendish
  [[122]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-conway-god-made-no-dead-thing), and came back in Fechner [[95]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#rom-fechner-1851-earth-more-alive-than-we).
  The turns are new answers added to the old ones, not replacements [[1]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-wil-no-era-has-one-definition).

## Open questions

- **When does pnoē become pneuma?** The Septuagint's breath of life is pnoē [[5]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-gen27-lxx-pnoe-not-pneuma), but
  Paul's life-giver is pneuma [[25]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-1cor15-psyche-zosa-pneuma-zoopoioun). Philo's *Questions on Genesis*
  now gives one step: the moulded man "obtained a soul by God breathing life into his face"
  [[123]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#wil2-philo-qg-life-breathed-into-face), but that text survives in Armenian and is read here in Latin, so it
  cannot show the Greek word. *Legum allegoriae* I.31–42, Philo's longer reading of the inbreathing, is held and unread.
- **Is the lamp Greek or Arabic?** Our pages show the Hippocratic heat
  [[124]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-hippocrates-growing-bodies-most-innate-heat) and the Latin radical moisture, but not the Arabic texts in
  between (Ibn Sīnā's *Canon* on al-ruṭūba al-aṣliyya). The one Canon manuscript claim is ◐ partial
  [[125]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-avicenna-canon-ms-life-force).
- **Bichat's definition** has a second, ◐ partial claim [[126]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-bichat-life-resists-death). The ✓ one
  [[77]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-bichat-1800-ensemble-des-fonctions) carries this page. Who before 1800 defined life against death?
  Wenzel says the same in the same year [[127]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-wenzel-1800-life-gradual-dying).
- **Does China have a turn of its own?** Zhuangzi's gathered qi [[20]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-zhuangzi-life-gathering-of-qi) still
  frames Zhu Xi's account of life fifteen centuries later [[128]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-zhuxi-life-is-jingqi-gathered) (◐ partial). That
  looks like continuity, not a turn. Neidan's essence → breath → spirit ladder [[129]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-jing-to-qi-to-shen-daoyan)
  may be the turn, but no claim dates it.
- **Is there a turn after 1930?** Our pages end with Whitehead [[106]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#wil-whitehead-life-bid-for-freedom) and Jung's
  libido as "life-energy" [[130]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#mod-jung-libido-energy-of-life-process-1921). Schrödinger, cybernetics and
  autopoiesis are not in the library yet.

title: 3. Making aliveness: how each era tried to create or prolong life
md:
**The question.** What did people at each point in history actually *do* to make themselves,
their things and their world more alive, or to keep them alive longer? And what did they think the practice
acted on: a heat, a moisture, a spirit, qi, prāṇa, a soul?

**The short answer.** A practice follows from a definition. Where life was a heat burning in a moisture, people
rationed the fuel. Where it was a spirit made of vapour, they fed it vapours. Where it was a food in the air,
they tried to catch the food. Where it was breath staying in the body, they held the breath. Where it was a soul
that could lodge in matter, they consecrated images. Quotes are Source Library's English unless the claim says
otherwise, each with its claim id and sourcelibrary.org/q/ link. ✓ claims are stated as fact; ◐ claims are
marked and hedged.

## The definitions the practices work on

- **A heat kept up.** Aristotle: "life is the maintenance of this heat" [[1]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#wil-aristotle-life-is-maintenance-of-heat)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhCV8opeqevMf7Pbdse); the animal is warm and moist, "and to live is to be of such
  a constitution, while old age is dry and cold, and so is a corpse" [[2]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-longitudine-to-live-is-to-be-warm-and-moist)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bkp1LfgqJZJGMHrwQkc). Roger Bacon adds that the heat consumes the moisture it
  lives on, "and thus it is the cause of extinguishing itself" [[3]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-bacon-heat-consumes-its-own-oil)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh9LDVEzhKX1hIfaQVm). The same texts make heat and moisture the soul's
  instrument, not the whole of life [[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-med-heat-moisture-is-instrument-not-definition); the practices work on
  the instrument.
- **A spirit made of vapour.** Ficino's spiritus is a "uapor quidã ſanguinis, purus, subtilis, calidus, & lucidus"
  [[5]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-spiritus-vapour-of-blood) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfLPSiUU6Nn085Z3ovN). A vapour can be fed.
- **Qi gathered.** Zhuangzi: "When it gathers, there is life; when it disperses, there is death"
  [[6]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-zhuangzi-life-gathering-of-qi) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiiqyDOxIbrfG74vX80). Zhu Xi seems to add
  that the quantity is finite, "人只有許多氣" (◐, our reading of the Chinese) [[7]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-zhuxi-life-is-jingqi-gathered)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0Z7VrdSkq9cVOvXc8).
- **Breath staying.** The Haṭhayogapradīpikā: "As long as the breath remains in the body, it is called life. Its
  departure is death. Therefore, one should restrain the breath" [[8]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-hyp-life-is-breath-staying)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BjlvoTqfGdnZcB6QepG).

All four make life a state you lose by spending, drying, dispersing or leaking [[9]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-asia-life-is-a-state-not-a-stuff).
That is why most practices before 1600 aim to *keep* life rather than add it.

## 1. Regimen and diet: tending a finite fire

**Acts on:** the innate heat and the radical moisture that feeds it.

**Greek and Galenic.** The Hippocratic Aphorisms feed the fire by age: the growing need much food, "In the
elderly, the heat is little; for this reason, they require little fuel, for it is extinguished by too much"
[[10]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-hippocrates-growing-bodies-most-innate-heat) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgToVOYIDLW73n7mrfI). The
*Regimen* made the soul itself a blend of fire and water, as Erastus quotes it in order to attack it
[[11]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-regimen-soul-blend-of-fire-and-water). Gerocomy, the care of the old, aims "to resist and prohibit the
body of the heart from drying out" [[12]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-gerocomy-galen) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhDcfI2n0zgaOHs41KG). Its
means were the six non-naturals: "air, food/drink, sleep/wakefulness, motion/rest, excretion/retention, and
passions of the mind" (SL's gloss on Horst's page) [[13]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-regimen-horst) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bg4FP6y7FDXJvgj62Hz).

**Medieval regimens.** The *Secretum secretorum*: whoever keeps "equality and temperance will receive healthy
salvation and length of days" [[14]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-secretum-temperance-length-of-days) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhE3Mf9pDQFgGdUUIeP).
Avicenna, as the *Regimen senum* quotes him, defines the art of health as guarding against putrefaction and
defending the moisture from dissolving too fast [[15]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-avicenna-art-of-health-defends-moisture). The same
*Regimen senum* (printed under Arnald's name, 1502) says old age's acceleration "can be delayed"
[[16]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-arnald-old-age-can-be-retarded) and names two routes: "One is the science of regimen. The other is the
science of the properties of certain things which the ancients concealed" [[17]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-arnald-two-doctrines-regimen-and-hidden-properties)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiQqBigh0DF2PuodfTT). The second route is section 3. The KB has no claim from the
Salernitan *Regimen sanitatis*.

**Roger Bacon** puts both routes in one book. Diet: "euchemic bread made from wheat which is preserved longer
generates a purer moisture", so the food's resistance to corruption passes into you, and some lands age men
faster [[18]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-bacon-keeping-foods-prolong-life) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh9LDVEzhKX1hIfaQVo); "we die sooner
than we ought" for want of regimen in youth [[19]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-prolongation-bacon) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhE2iLlPTWz8GX5iAQQ).
Medicine: he reports a man who took a medicine and "looked like a man of thirty years" [[20]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-bacon-great-prolongation-possible)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh9LDVEzhKX1hIfaQXK).

**Exercise and measure.** Mercuriale (1569): in summer "the native heat must be more greatly excited by exercise
so that it may digest more properly" [[21]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-mercuriale-exercise-excites-native-heat)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BeqTVJHMmnkCxbzrxul). Cornaro's sober life (1558) weighs it: at 78 his daily food
"was exactly weighed at twelve ounces, I increased it by two ounces to fourteen", and within ten days he fell
ill [[22]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-cornaro-two-ounces-nearly-killed) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhDbCqNu0xst9DsV8CB). Readers kept the
numbers: Wolff cites his cure at 87 [[23]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-sober-life-wolff).

**Francis Bacon** (1623) changes the premise. In youth "the Matter of Repair might be almost eternal, if the
Manner of Repair did not fail" [[24]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-fbacon-repair-almost-eternal) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejuAwFkHJuSIes77U9).
The agent of decay is the spirit itself, "instar Flammæ lenis, per- petuò prædatorius" [[25]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-fbacon-spirit-gentle-flame-predatory)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh9KsAKy8yYv6VJ40KV), so he cools and condenses it, with nitre and with the scent "of
pure and good earth, recently dug up and turned over" [[26]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-fbacon-condense-spirits-opium-nitre-earth)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejuAwFkHJuSIes77Xn).

**Hufeland.** The KB holds only reception, a 1798 gazette praising "The Art of Prolonging Human Life by Hufeland"
[[27]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-makrobiotik-arcana) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNfN07BdVwQKjhABuA); the claims about what the book
prescribes are unverified and not used. The period's model is on another page: if life is Lebenskraft put into
activity, it is "zugleich ein allmähliges Sterben" [[28]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-wenzel-1800-life-gradual-dying)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhtHceBAv3sXXSkgZjf). That is the old lamp with a new word for the oil.

**China.** The *Suwen* (◐, our reading of the Chinese) praises the ancients who ate and drank in measure and kept
regular hours, so body and spirit stayed together for a hundred years [[29]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-suwen-shanggu-tianzhen-regimen)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0RjtX6Qv4WGgPyF9g). Ge Hong blames those who refuse yangsheng, "choosing instead
to whittle it down, torment it, exhaust it, and drain it dry" [[30]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-yangsheng-hong)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgScPs1ZOzwVYOWC8Ic). Ears, eyes and mouth are "the apertures of jing essence",
shen and qi, to be kept closed [[31]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-three-treasures-apertures) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl15LeTfmsvPk8vXH2A):
life kept by stopping leaks. Grain avoidance belongs here too [[32]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-bigu-shouzhong). Two voices push against
technique. Mencius: "let there be no assisting the growth of that nature" [[33]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-mencius-no-assisting-growth)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BilNuXPGh197Rlit5Dm). Li Yu (1730): "I place the pursuit of joy first"
[[34]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-yangsheng-yu) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BijB41gpbmeF0lp4A0p).

## 2. Feeding the spirit: Ficino's diet of vapours

**Acts on:** spiritus, the warm, bright vapour of the blood.

Ficino's *De vita* (1489) is SL's fullest text on drawing life in. Its precepts avoid "resolution" on one side and
"suffocation and putrefaction" on the other [[35]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-prolongation-ficino) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNkmskNpYW9SLrUrob).
Scholars need it most: each is "totus est fermè spiritus", almost wholly spirit [[36]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-scholars-almost-wholly-spirit)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfLPSiUU6Nn085Z3ozI).

- **Wine, scent, song, light.** "wine acts as earth; the very scent of wine performs the role of water; song and
  sound move the air; and light represents the fiery element" [[37]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-four-nourishments-of-spirit)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfLPSiUU6Nn085Z3ozI). Wine "restores the natural humor, fosters internal heat",
  undiluted for cold old men [[38]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-undiluted-wine-softens-cold-age) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BeiybVV2XaXMYfWtoBq).
  Odours feed the spirit because both are vapour, "et simile simili nutriatur" [[39]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-odours-feed-spirit-of-old)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfLPSiUU6Nn085Z3oww).
- **Gold and gems.** Glowing gold quenched in spring water, gold leaf in the drink [[40]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-quench-gold-in-water);
  gold, coral, silk and gems dilate and illuminate the spirit [[41]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-gold-gems-gather-illuminate-spirit).
- **Green things.** The old should "frequently spend time among green and sweet-smelling plants. For these,
  being living and breathing, breathe forth their essence to increase the spirit" [[42]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-green-plants-breathe-into-spirit)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BeiybVV2XaXMYfWtoC2). "their essence" is SL's addition; the Latin says the plants
  breathe out, breath feeding breath. Green works because in it "the indwelling light of the sun still retains a
  youthful moisture" [[43]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-green-holds-vernal-moisture) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BeiybVV2XaXMYfWtoC7).
- **Young blood.** "Cur non & nostri senes omni uidelicet auxilio destituti, sanguinem adolescentis sugant?"
  Why should old men not suck the blood of a willing, healthy, cheerful youth [[44]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-old-suck-young-blood)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfLPSiUU6Nn085Z3owZ). Blood is the matter of spirit, so life can be transferred.
- **The world's spirit.** The world is animated "multoq; efficacius" than any animal, and by applying our spirit
  to it "per artem physicam affectumq;" heavenly goods pass into soul and body [[45]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-world-animated-spirit-applied)
  (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfLPSiUU6Nn085Z3oxV).

The logic outlives Ficino: a half-satirical 1744 treatise takes up the claim that Hermippus "owed his Vivacity to
the Nourishment he received from the Breath of Girls" [[46]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-cohausen-1744-breath-of-girls)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BftPvSBP6kVMlREThTY).

## 3. Elixirs, quintessence, potable gold, and the food of life in the air

**Acts on:** first corruption (the elixir preserves), then the radical moisture renamed balsam, then a
life-substance spread through the world.

**Quintessence.** Rupescissa (c. 1351): "the heaven of the human being, which alchemists strive for, for the
preservation of all qualities of the human body" [[47]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-rupescissa-quintessence-heaven-of-human-body)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgxWyOpVhDxJxD37R4M). Pseudo-Lull: "it preserves flesh from corruption,
strengthens the elemental nature, restores original youth, vivifies the spirit" [[48]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-lull-quintessence-restores-youth)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhbmVHgYBqDDKixXoe3). It was drawn from aqua vitae [[49]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-edge-water-of-life-descends-quintessence).
Rejuvenation comes as a consequence of preservation [[50]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-alch-elixir-preserves-rather-than-vivifies). By 1572
the name is fixed: "It takes away all the illnesses of old age, and therefore it is called the Elixir vitae"
[[51]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-elixir-ulstad) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bht5tvtmRq9gY1UZ8hh).

**Paracelsus** redefines life to fit: "life is nothing else but a certain Balsamic Mummy" [[52]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#wil-paracelsus-life-is-balsamic-mummy)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfyLdDLIMDAGQePf0lj), what keeps the body from rotting. *De vita longa* divides
medicine in two, "one, so that it may be preserved; the other, so that what has been lost may be restored"
[[53]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-paracelsus-vita-longa-twofold-medicine) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfyLdDLIMDAGQePf0lT). Croll (1609)
names the continuity with the physicians: "Moisture, Vital Balsam, and the most precious Nectar of our Life" are
one thing [[54]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-croll-radical-moisture-vital-balsam-nectar) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BfiMcbiKLh4yw5ikRgO).

**Potable gold.** Libavius (1607) defends Paracelsus, "who claimed that life could be prolonged by potable gold"
[[55]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-libavius-potable-gold-can-prolong-life) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BekQ5fJVi5JQMjMomEz). Anthony (1610)
argues in Galenic terms: gold serves "the heart, which is the domicile of life" [[56]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-anthony-gold-for-heart-domicile-of-life)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhPRWtdvI5DPVlr1nua). It was contested from the start: "Aurum potabile [potable
gold] is nonsense" (Reusner, 1582) [[57]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-aurum-potabile-reusner) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNCMBzD41TZJkbLI31).

**The food of life in the air.** Around 1600 the source of life moves outside the body. Paracelsus: "NO man can
deny that Aire gives life to all things" [[58]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-paracelsus-air-gives-life-life-spiritual-essence)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BekIYFS7EoKqXHwqdbX). Sendivogius (1604): "Man, created from the earth, lives from
the air: for there is in the air a hidden food of life" [[59]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-sendivogius-hidden-food-of-life-in-air-latin)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/u1g2D4Gm56LDuQpg9uYGcGJljB). Fludd and Digby repeat the dictum in the weapon-salve
quarrel [[60]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-fludd-grain-of-life-volatile-salt-of-air), [[61]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-digby-hidden-food-of-life-in-air). Glauber
(1659): "life is invisibly dispersed within it, like a little salt in much water" [[62]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-glauber-life-dispersed-in-air-like-salt)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNf6YjVsQAbBLZN89w), and "The air receives its food of life from the sun, and the
sun from GOD" [[63]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-glauber-medicine-without-life-cannot-heal) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNf6YjVsQAbBLZN89x).
The practical change is that a medicine must itself be made alive by exposure to air.

**China.** Ge Hong's golden elixir transfers incorruptibility: gold and cinnabar "refine the human body, and can
thus cause a person never to age and never to die. This is indeed borrowing external substances to strengthen
oneself" [[64]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-baopuzi-jindan-borrowed-incorruptibility) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgScPs1ZOzwVYOWC8IY).
Later the elixir moves inward: "Vital breath is the inner elixir [nèidān], while medicinal compound is the outer
elixir [wàidān]" [[65]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-neidan-x-2) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgSdQUjYnHxx7pGNNiV).

**India and Tibet.** Caraka: "those devoted to rasāyana lived for thousands of years without aging, weakness,
exhaustion, or death" [[66]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-rasayana-charaka) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BikGiuGd2JWxn8v9mE9). Rasāyana
generates ojas [[67]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-edge-rasayana-cultivates-ojas), and in the Rasaratnākara it is "the cause of long life on
earth once the mercury is perfected" [[68]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-rasayana-nagarjuna) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bi6NL9v0m8c2vRwrBwp).
A Tibetan chülen taken with milk "doubles the lifespan" [[69]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-chulen-anonymous-3) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BoVJLM72I2CIdCYP7vE).
A Buddhist page in the Tengyur sets the limit: "the capacity of rejuvenation therapy is strictly limited"
[[70]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-rasayana-anonymous) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BoVGtTvLmBBlYEO9ucl).

## 4. Breath: holding life in

**Acts on:** the breath itself (vāyu, qi, rlung), and through it the mind and the inner heat.

**Background in the West.** Genesis gives the breath *of* life, "ויפח באפיו נשמת חיים" [[71]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-gen27-nishmat-hayyim-nefesh-hayyah)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejgbOGZRXGHekUk8a4), breath as carrier rather than life itself [[72]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-anc-breath-of-life-is-not-life).
Tertullian defines living as breathing: "Quid est non uiuere: flatum, opinor, ex semetipso non agere"
[[73]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-tertullian-to-breathe-is-to-live) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhK94js5iwV2Lp3ptod). For Galen breath
serves heat: respiration's first use is "the preservation of the innate heat" [[74]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-galen-respiration-guards-innate-heat)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhEv2lngIbB5YkT13R5). The West had a breathing definition of life, but apart from the
Hermippus "Breath of Girls" [[46]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-cohausen-1744-breath-of-girls), the KB holds no Western breathing practice to prolong it.

**India.** Patañjali: prāṇāyāma is "the regulation of the flow of inhalation and exhalation" [[75]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-pranayama-patanjali)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTYVpZubNsRTOyWIsR). The Haṭhayogapradīpikā turns the definition of life into the
method (restrain the breath, since life is its staying) [[8]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-hyp-life-is-breath-staying), and ties it to the
mind: "When the breath moves, the mind moves. When the breath is still, the mind becomes still"
[[76]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-hyp-breath-moves-mind-moves) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BjlvoTqfGdnZcB6QepG). Of absolute retention:
"Nothing in the three worlds is difficult for him to obtain" [[77]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-hyp-kevala-kumbhaka)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BjlvoTqfGdnZcB6Qepr).

**China.** "The reason humans do not die lies within Embryonic Breathing" [[78]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-taixi-masters)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BeuoM3Qf1PUZMCAKmc7). Ge Hong: "Return the essence and practice embryonic breathing;
prolong life without end" [[79]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-taixi-hong-2) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgScPs1ZOzwVYOWC8IA). By 1615 "It
is called Embryonic Breathing [Taixi] in name, but in reality it is the Inner Elixir" [[80]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-neidan-zhenren)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BkB9QcpJHEtIiMDHYZq). Zhang Boduan warns against forcing it: "Some accumulate cold
breath and turn it into illness" [[81]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-taixi-boduan) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BkB67Rd3IXUdf0hqLuU).

**Tibet.** When the winds stop moving, "the caṇḍālī [inner heat; tummo] blazes from the navel" [[82]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-tummo-anonymous-3)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BoUlYmyA5KBBdAb1udJ): breath held becomes heat. Longevity liturgies call back what
has declined: "Summon back the soul-longevity that has declined!" [[83]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-bla-tshe-two-renderings)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BijgQuLReT57JctPKUF).

**New Thought (1900s).** W. W. Atkinson, writing as Yogi Ramacharaka, calls prāṇa "the Sanskrit term meaning
“Absolute Energy.”" [[84]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-ramacharaka-prana-absolute-energy) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgQrmvo8gdwpMlkge7J),
a reading the yoga texts held do not support [[85]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-asia-energy-gloss-has-a-date). His healing manual gives a
practice for producing the feeling itself: "Rub the hands to-gether briskly for a few minutes, and then swing them
to-and-fro a little while, until they have that undefinable feeling of "aliveness" and be-ing full of Energy"
[[86]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#mod-ramacharaka-hands-aliveness-1906) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgQro6KhYX2AEbzkloy). Under his own name:
"Now I wish to put LIFE into you" [[87]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#mod-atkinson-put-life-into-you-1906) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOY6Bs2ApAjJ0okbzN).
On SL's pages the English noun for a felt aliveness arrives through these writers [[88]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-mod-aliveness-is-a-new-thought-word).

## 5. Making things alive

**Acts on:** a soul, spirit or divine presence lodged in prepared matter; or a life that survives in seed, ash or
blood.

**Animated statues.** Augustine transmits the Hermetic *Asclepius* on "Statues animated, full of sense and
spirit, doing such great and many things; statues with foreknowledge of the future" [[89]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-animated-statues-augustine)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOcTYlpYt1I5kS3cw0). Proclus explains the telestic art: things made "from partial
and perishable matter are made suitable through certain symbols to share in god, to be moved by him, and to
foretell the future" [[90]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-animated-statues-proclus) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhF7QJ6gMThjDrVTgSM). Matter
fitted by symbols receives what it resembles.

**Talismans and images.** The *Picatrix* says the making "must be according to the reality of nature"
[[91]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-talismans-al) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BelEaq07BrrGrMhHTOc). In the 1582 French Ficino, when we make
images well and attend to the work, our spirit "joins itself to the stars with the Spirit of the World"
[[92]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-spiritus-mundi-ficino) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhtEJFxl8oBMEIH2YRJ). Agrippa's rule: gather
scattered things that conform to one star, and "a singular gift is soon poured in from that Idea", through the
world soul [[93]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-gift-via-world-soul-prepared-matter) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bg4FPHKlPIdDUKZgnnq).

**Consecration.** Tibetan consecration (rab gnas) is "the act of summoning and causing the syllable Hum to enter
and remain firm" [[94]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-consecration-anonymous) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BoUzfmY0wSsIQFL7D90), an "excellent
abiding" [[95]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-consecration-anonymous-2). A tantra attributed to Śaṅkara has one perform "the prāṇapratiṣṭhā
[infusion of life]" in the vessel (◐) [[96]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-consecration-shankaracharya). Life is installed, and the test is
that it stays.

**Making people from maize: the Popol Vuh.** The K'iche' Popol Vuh is the only text on this page in which the
makers are gods and the made thing is the human race, told by the people themselves. The gods try four times. The
mud body "was soft, compressed, and limp; it simply crumbled and became wet". The wooden people speak and multiply,
"however, they turned out foolish, without hearts and without understanding. And so they did not remember their
creator anymore" [[97]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/americas#world-maya-popol-vuh-four-tries) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bn0a1fFYMTCEUIROCi6). The K'iche'
has *macu habi quigux*, "they had no heart (k'u'x)". The people who live are ground from maize: "Only yellow corn and
white corn were their flesh; only food became the arms and legs of the men" [[98]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/americas#world-maya-popol-vuh-maize-flesh)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bn0a1fFYMTCEUIROCj3). There is no breath blown into clay, as in Genesis 2:7. The test
of success is not that the thing moves (the wooden people move) but that it has a heart that remembers and addresses
its makers. Life is the right substance plus a relation. See page 5, §A.

**Golem and homunculus.** Allix (1707) reports that Jews "make an image of clay like a human being, whisper or
murmur some conjurations into its ears, and the image walks" [[99]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-golem-allix) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhrYtdr1bRaTY4ZUPIG).
Sennert reports the Paracelsian method by which a homunculus "may be generated without father and mother, by the
benefit of the Chemical art" [[100]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-homunculus-sennert) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOdUYtxFzheCvy8Ryk);
opponents called it among "the filths of Paracelsian impiety" [[101]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-edge-homunculus-belongs-paracelsianism). The
recipe rests on the maxim that "nothing is ever born or grows, nor does anything possess a soul and life, except
after putrefaction"
[[102]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-turba-arnold-no-soul-and-life-except-after-putrefaction) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNeth0pF9COA22wrop).
Redi (1668) tested the premise with sealed vessels: from corpses, "if the seed is not brought upon them, no animal
of any kind is ever born" [[103]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-redi-no-animal-from-corpses-without-seed) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhIGDSedxFvaQIfptkV).

**Palingenesis of plants.** Browne (1642): "This I make good by experience, and can from the ashes of a plant
revive the plant" [[104]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-browne-revive-plant-from-its-ashes) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOdNSwxzQzGhq5jH8Q).
A Cracow physician, reported third-hand, kept plant ashes sealed in glass and preserved "their spirits—the authors
of all their faculties" [[105]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-tachenius-quercetanus-palingenesis-cracow) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BftPw7llU2XSsAZEIlI).
What survives the fire is the spirit, so the form can be called back.

**Life at a distance.** Burggrav's lamp, made from a man's blood, "burns continuously as long as the man from
whose blood it is prepared draws vital Spirit" [[106]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-burggrav-lamp-of-life-from-blood)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNfEbV88bRSfXzqWpk); the Latin idiom means only that he is still breathing. The
weapon-salve was "smeared only onto a cloth or a bloody sword" to cure a patient "many miles away"
[[107]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-weapon-salve-saltzmann) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BlQdbg43Icbi1xCt8nX). In Melanesia a stone shaped like
a yam is buried among the yams and a good harvest "is attributed to the mana possessed by the said stone"
[[108]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-farrow-mana-yam-stone) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bjeab2Id6kN1bhmInvx).

**The machine turns the question round.** Hobbes: "seeing life is but a motion of Limbs", "why may we not say,
that all Automata" have "an artificiall life?" [[109]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-hobbes-life-is-motion-of-limbs)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOdkuOeBegxKcukcZj). If life is motion from an inner spring, a made thing is alive
by construction, and no consecration is needed [[110]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-descartes-clocks-fountains-mills).

## 6. Places: green things, genii and land-spirits

**Acts on:** the spirit, through air and greenness; or a resident spirit of the place, owed offerings.

**Green and healthy places.** Before Ficino's green plants, Hildegard (c. 1150): "The herbs drink in this
greenness as strongly as a lamb drinks milk" [[111]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-hildegard-herbs-suck-viriditas) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Belt7NEGUjG0kcz3o2v).
Roger Bacon's choice of a land where foods keep [[18]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-bacon-keeping-foods-prolong-life) and Francis Bacon's
fresh-dug earth [[26]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-fbacon-condense-spirits-opium-nitre-earth) make place part of regimen. Paracelsus:
"Wherever, however, the nature of the place and the body meet together, there it is arrived at the 600th year
with no trouble" [[112]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-paracelsus-vita-longa-600-years-place-and-body) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhbmkgbHy2VoQyn7wV2).

**The genius loci.** A 1558 commentary quotes Virgil's Aeneas, who binds his temples with a leafy branch "And
prays to the genius of the place, and to Earth, the first of gods" [[113]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-genius-loci-manuzio)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BjdnnIrXKvwssxw8hXl). A 1688 dissertation says the ancients gave a genius to "every
kingdom, province, region, city, and people", "promoting good things for it and averting evils" [[114]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-genius-loci-wagner)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhNfEvitZy5Nw5RqS0i). Wissowa ties the word to begetting, "the root gen, gignere"
[[115]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-wissowa-genius-gignere) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRqf3nKEkA365Xn0mt). The household cult had its
shrine: Alexander Severus "performed divine service in his own Lararium" [[116]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-offerings-pontano)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BhCvfyNb6w6al3XhdUL).

**Offerings to land-spirits.** Han Yu at Chaozhou: "the spirits of the mountains and rivers provide protection to
the people; the officials shall establish shrines and halls" [[117]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-shanchuan-zhishen-hanyu)
(https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bl0TqEzASLI6rCgiUVe). A Nyingma tantra names "The King of Land-spirits" and the harms
of placing a rite wrongly toward him [[118]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-sadag-land-spirit-king) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BijRSV1S9SxUxGL6qER).
Plutarch gives the land a breath of its own, an "enthusiastic exhalation" that serves prophecy
[[119]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-plutarch-oracle-enthusiastic-exhalation) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgSh3NmTrRCQhPkUbXl). Tylor finds it
hard to say whether a sacred tree is "inhabited, like a man, by its own proper life or soul" or possessed by
another spirit [[120]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-tylor-tree-own-life-or-soul) (https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOfaINf9HwhvX4AslR). Here the
place is not made alive. It already is, and the work is to stand rightly toward it.

**Buildings: no evidence.** Han Yu's halls [[117]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-shanchuan-zhishen-hanyu) and the lararium [[116]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-offerings-pontano)
are buildings made *for* a living presence; that is as close as the KB comes. No claim treats the design of a
building or garden as making a place more alive. Christopher Alexander is not on Source Library
(his books are not held and are in copyright), so an account of aliveness in architecture
has to cite him from outside SL. Leibniz's "garden full of plants" is a figure for matter, not a practice
[[121]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-leibniz-garden-full-of-plants).

## What changed over time

1. **From tending a finite store to drawing life from the world.** Medieval regimen rations a fire that consumes
   its own oil [[3]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#med-bacon-heat-consumes-its-own-oil), and the early elixir only preserves
   [[50]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-alch-elixir-preserves-rather-than-vivifies). Ficino feeds the spirit from wine, song, light, plants and
   the world's spirit [[37]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-four-nourishments-of-spirit), [[45]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-world-animated-spirit-applied);
   around 1600 the alchemists find "a hidden food of life" in the air [[59]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/alchemy-medicine#alch-sendivogius-hidden-food-of-life-in-air-latin).
   China moves the other way, from swallowing gold to refining breath [[65]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-neidan-x-2).
2. **From fuel to repair, and back to a stock.** Francis Bacon recasts ageing as failed repair
   [[24]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-fbacon-repair-almost-eternal); around 1800 living again spends a stock [[28]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-wenzel-1800-life-gradual-dying),
   and Bichat defines life as "l’ensemble des fonctions qui résistent à la mort" [[122]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-bichat-1800-ensemble-des-fonctions).
3. **From installing a soul to building a mechanism.** Statues and golems receive life by symbol or word (the Popol Vuh's makers, by material and by heart [[98]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/americas#world-maya-popol-vuh-maize-flesh))
   [[90]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-animated-statues-proclus), [[99]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-golem-allix); after Hobbes a self-moving engine counts as
   "an artificiall life" [[109]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#ems-hobbes-life-is-motion-of-limbs).
4. **From a substance to a felt quality.** By 1906 the practice is to rub the hands until they feel "aliveness"
   [[86]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/modern#mod-ramacharaka-hands-aliveness-1906). The thing acted on is a sensation, not a heat or a breath.
5. **What stayed.** The inhabited land: genii and mountain spirits are honoured, not made
   [[114]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-genius-loci-wagner), [[117]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/animism-ethnography#anim-shanchuan-zhishen-hanyu).

## Critiques that bear on this page

- *Life force* and *vital energy* in SL's English are mostly glosses on narrower words (breath, wind, heat)
  [[123]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-cmp-life-force-is-a-gloss-layer), [[124]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-ren-vital-force-glosses).
- *The life of metals* is several things, not one doctrine [[125]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-alch-life-of-metals-metaphor-or-doctrine).
- The library leans to 16th–17th-century editions, which swells the Ficino-to-Glauber middle.

## Open questions

- **Hufeland's *Makrobiotik*:** a page from the book itself, before saying what it prescribes [[27]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-makrobiotik-arcana).
- **The Salernitan *Regimen sanitatis*:** no claim yet.
- **A Western breath practice before 1900:** is there one on SL? Galen's respiration [[74]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-galen-respiration-guards-innate-heat)
  and the Hermippus treatise [[46]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-cohausen-1744-breath-of-girls) are the nearest.
- **Ficino's talismans:** claims from the Latin *De vita* III, not only the 1582 French [[92]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-spiritus-mundi-ficino).
- **Indian consecration:** a primary Āgama or Purāṇa page to firm up the ◐ prāṇapratiṣṭhā claim [[96]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/asian#asia-consecration-shankaracharya).
- **Gardens and buildings:** any SL text that designs a place to make people more alive, rather than sending them
  to green places [[42]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-green-plants-breathe-into-spirit)? If none, Alexander's question has no premodern
  source on SL.

title: 4. Life as soul: anima, psychē, the world soul, Aristotle's kinds of soul
md:
**The question.** For most of history, "what is alive?" was answered with another question: what has soul?
To be alive (ἔμψυχος, *animatus*, *beseelt*) was to be *ensouled*. This page follows that answer: Aristotle's
ladder of souls; the world soul, which made the cosmos itself a living thing; the words different languages used
for soul; and the point in the 17th century where "soul" and "life" came apart.

**How to read it.** Every claim cited is ✓ verified on a Source Library page unless marked ◐. Quotes are SL's
English (a model translation of the page) unless the original is given. Each quote carries its claim id and the
page's shortlink. All claims on this page are tagged `thread:soul`.

---

## A. Aristotle's ladder: plant ⊂ animal ⊂ human

**Soul is what makes a body alive.** Aristotle starts *On the Soul* II by marking off the ensouled from the
unsouled "by the presence of life." The defining move is that life is not one thing. "Living" is said in many
ways, and having any one of them is enough to count as alive:

> "Since "living" is said in many ways, if even one of these exists, we say the thing is alive: such as intellect,
> sensation, local movement and rest, and furthermore…" [[1]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-ensouled-distinguished-by-living)
> https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjcdeEm3cWUjzPEEX
> (πλεοναχῶς δὲ τοῦ ζῆν λεγομένου, κἂν ἕν τι τούτων ἐνυπάρχῃ μόνον, ζῆν αὐτό φαμεν)

The soul is no extra thing inside the body. It is the body's form, the "first entelechy" (first actuality) of a
natural organic body [[2]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-soul-first-entelechy-organic-body): "that by which we live, perceive, and think
primarily" [[3]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-soul-that-by-which-we-live-perceive-think). It "is not a body, but it is something of a
body" (σῶμα μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ἔστι, σώματος δέ τι) [[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-soul-not-a-body-but-of-a-body)
https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjcdeEm3cWUjzPEEY.

**The nested ladder.** Each soul contains the one below it. A higher soul does not sit on top of a lower one. It
includes it.

- **Plant: the nutritive (vegetative) soul.** Its powers are to feed, grow and reproduce. "Plants possess only the
  nutritive" (ὑπάρχει δὲ τοῖς μὲν φυτοῖς τὸ θρεπτικὸν μόνον) [[5]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-plants-nutritive-only-animals-touch).
  It is "the first and most common faculty of the soul, according to which life belongs to all"
  [[6]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-deanima-nutritive-soul-first-and-most-common) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjcdeEm3cWUjzPEEZ. Avicenna's
  Latin splits it into three powers, the nutritive, the augmentative and the generative: "The nutritive is like the
  beginning, and the generative is like the end" [[7]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-avicenna-three-vegetative-powers)
  https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Beol2PCFaiTjSNsTQde.
  - **Animal: plus the sensitive soul.** Its powers are sensation (at least touch), appetite, and in some animals
    local motion. "If it has the sensitive, it also has the appetitive" [[5]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-plants-nutritive-only-animals-touch)
    https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjcdeEm3cWUjzPEEY. Aquinas sorts the grades: plants have only nourishment;
    "sense is found in them without local motion, as in imperfect animals like oysters"; local motion comes with
    the "perfect animals" [[8]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-aquinas-grades-of-living-plants-oysters-ox) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPwsyqYIuMRK0H613F.
    - **Human: plus the rational (intellective) soul.** Its powers are thinking and intellect. Reason comes
      "finally, and least commonly": "those mortal beings that possess calculation also possess all the others"
      [[9]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-reason-last-and-rarest-has-all) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjcdeEm3cWUjzPEEZ.
      Aristotle leaves room above: "such as humans and if there is any other such thing, or even something more
      honorable" [[10]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-intellect-in-humans-or-higher).

**The ladder line itself: the triangle in the square.**

> "for the prior always exists potentially in that which follows, both in the case of shapes and in the case of
> living things, such as the triangle in the square, or the nutritive in the sensitive."
> [[11]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-ar-deanima-triangle-in-square-nutritive-in-sensitive) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjcdeEm3cWUjzPEEY
> (ἀεὶ γὰρ ἐν τῷ ἐφεξῆς ὑπάρχει δυνάμει τὸ πρότερον … οἷον ἐν τετραγώνῳ μὲν τρίγωνον, ἐν αἰσθητικῷ δὲ τὸ θρεπτικόν.)

The line does not reverse: "the vegetative can exist without the sensitive, as in plants, and not the reverse"
(*vegetatiua potest esse absque sensitiva. ut in plantis et non econuerso*), from the school florilegium of
*auctoritates* [[12]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-auctoritates-four-powers-not-conversely) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPvCZzOCP8ath3QV3j.

**How the commentators made it a ladder of living things.**
- **Versor's 1496 text** prints the line as the schools read it: "As in the square, there is the triangle; in the
  sensitive, the vegetative" [[13]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-versor-1496-tetragon-line) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPx1wsCIigge7e7Dlt.
- **Lambertus de Monte** turns the geometry into arithmetic: "the superior number includes the inferior; therefore,
  the superior soul includes the inferior" [[14]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-lambertus-higher-soul-includes-lower-as-number)
  https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPwJUvrF07qEFELBsJ.
- **Aquinas** extends the figures to an open series, "the triangle is prior to the tetragon, and the tetragon
  before the pentagon" [[15]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-aquinas-no-soul-apart-from-the-kinds). He reads Aristotle's purpose as
  distinguishing the modes of living along with the grades of the living (*distinguere modos viuendi cum gradus
  viuentium*) [[8]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-aquinas-grades-of-living-plants-oysters-ox).
- **The Avicennan definition.** A living body "is distinguished from a non-living body by its soul, and not by its
  body" [[16]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#wil2-avicenna-living-body-differs-by-soul-first-perfection) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Beol2PCFaiTjSNsTQdR.
  The 1546 edition's notes define each of the three souls as a "first perfection", the intellectual one taking in
  the operations of all those below [[17]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-avicenna-three-souls-each-first-perfection) ◐ *(medium confidence:
  the notes attribute the definitions to "the Arabic authors", not to Avicenna's own chapter)*. They rank the
  rational power "in the third order … less common" than the motive and the apprehensive powers
  [[18]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-avicenna-gloss-three-orders-common-to-proper).
- **A Christian version.** Gregory of Nyssa reads the same three grades into Paul's body, soul and spirit: "calling
  the nourishing part the 'body,' signifying the sensing part by the 'soul,' and the intellectual by the 'spirit'"
  [[19]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/hebrew-christian#heb-nyssa-body-soul-spirit-are-life-grades) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgUu8L0PPaSB6cFJwaO.
- **The ladder survives into the 19th century, with its rungs renamed.** In Fechner's 1848 version the animal "must
  be content with vital force and soul; the plant … with mere vital force; the crystal … is entirely dead"
  [[20]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#rom-fechner-1848-ladder-lebenskraft-soul-spirit) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOcWgAfDFur4esBIQE.

**A finding.** In the 1500 Latin edition, a marginal note reads *in alatis* ("in winged things") where the text has
*in animatis*. SL's English duly reads "In figures and in winged things, as in a tetragon there is a trigon"
[[21]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/medieval#soul-ar-moerbeke-1500-animatis-read-as-winged) (tagged `mistranslation`).

**Critique.** Entelechy is not an agent: Aristotle's soul is the body's *being* alive, not a thing that animates it
from outside [[22]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-anc-entelechy-is-not-an-agent). Later "vital principle" readings import an agent that the
Greek does not have.

## B. The world soul: the cosmos as a living thing, Plato to Fechner

If soul is what makes a body alive, a cosmos that moves itself and generates life must have one. One step per
figure:

1. **Plato, *Timaeus* 30b, 34b (c. 360 BCE).** The cosmos is "a living creature, endowed with soul and intelligence"
   (ζῷον ἔμψυχον ἔννουν) [[23]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-timaeus-cosmos-zoon-empsychon-ennoun) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjaajFkkigTWDq15T.
   The craftsman "placed the soul in the center of it and extended it through the whole, and also covered the
   body with it from the outside" [[24]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-wo-timaeus-soul-set-in-middle-stretched-through)
   https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgTjaajFkkigTWDq15X. In Cicero's Latin it becomes *hunc mundum animal esse*
   [[25]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-cicero-timaeus-hunc-mundum-animal-esse).
2. **The Stoics (SVF II).** There is one scale for all bodies: hexis (cohesion) holds stones and wood, physis
   (nature) grows plants, and psychē (soul) animates animals (ἕξεως μὲν ὡς λίθοι καὶ ξύλα, φύσεως δὲ καθάπερ τὰ φυτά,
   ψυχῆς δὲ τὰ ζῶα). The world, which is "a body of unified things" that suffers as a whole, is held together by
   soul, not by mere hexis [[26]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#wil2-stoic-cosmos-held-by-soul-not-hexis) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bh4JoOM2z0Yjwt90uqG;
   see also [[27]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-stoic-hexis-physis-psyche-grades). Cicero's Stoic: "It is therefore absurd to say, when men and
   beasts are held by this heat … that the world is without sense" [[28]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-cicero-nd-world-animans-by-self-moving-heat)
   https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BjbwFWUl1YjsLz3tBGd.
3. **Plotinus (c. 250).** He reverses the picture: soul is not in the cosmos, the cosmos is in soul, "and no part of
   it is destitute of soul; being moistened with life, like a net in water" [[29]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#soul-wo-plotinus-cosmos-net-in-sea-of-soul)
   https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bi8TYwtni7t7sPx5opi. "All are parts of one universal animal"
   [[30]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-plotinus-universe-one-animal). Proclus reads the world soul as "life and continuity and life-generation"
   (ζωογονία) [[31]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-proclus-world-soul-zoogonia).
4. **Ficino (1482, 1489).** *Theologia Platonica*: "that the celestial spheres have souls, not only the Platonists
   but all the Peripatetics as well confess" (*Cæleſtes ſphæras habere animas…*) [[32]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#soul-wo-ficino-tp-spheres-ensouled)
   https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Beuqp8OU09pFkQW68ja. *De vita* III: "the worldly body, as far as appears from its
   motion and generation, is alive everywhere" (*mundanum corpus … est ubique uiuum*)
   [[33]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#soul-wo-ficino-devita-world-body-alive-everywhere) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BiPvvE2Bhoabi19BZc5. The
   world's spirit is "animated, just as any animal is, and much more effectively", and our spirit can be applied to
   it by art [[34]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-ficino-world-animated-spirit-applied).
5. **Agrippa (1533).** "It would be absurd if … flies and little worms were worthy of life and possessed souls, yet
   the world itself …" did not [[35]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-absurd-that-world-not-live)
   https://sourcelibrary.org/q/Bg4FP6y7FDXJvgj8EgI. The world soul's power spreads through all things by the fifth
   essence: "nothing is found in the whole world that lacks a spark of its power" (*nihil enim reperitur … quod suæ
   uirtutis scintilla careat*) [[36]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-quintessence-spark-in-all-things).
6. **Bruno (1584).** "with greater ease the World Soul rules the universe than our soul rules our body"
   [[37]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-bruno-world-soul-rules-without-bond) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejgTOg3pxq9OAd9Ss3.
7. **Patrizi (1591).** In his *Pampsychia* every soul comes from intellect, so "no soul is by its nature irrational"
   [[38]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-patrizi-no-soul-irrational) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgRAcz4u5rRizg0PB1Y. Gilbert (1600) gives the
   magnet's version: it is "pitiable" to deny soul to the stars and the earth "while it is granted to the worm, the
   ant" [[39]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-gilbert-soulless-stars-below-the-worm).
8. **Henry More (1659/1662).** The world soul survives as a lesser thing: "The Spirit of Nature, or the inferiour
   Soul of the World" [[40]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#soul-wo-more-spirit-of-nature-inferior-world-soul) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejWIDHvgIoRz3OeuNo.
   It is "A substance incorporeal, but without Sense and Animadversion, pervading the whole Matter of the Universe,
   and exercising a Plastical power therein" [[41]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/early-modern-science#soul-wo-more-spirit-of-nature-defined)
   https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BejWIDHvgIoRz3OeuNn.
9. **Schelling, *Von der Weltseele* (1798).** One principle "links the whole of nature into a universal organism",
   and he recognises in it what "the most ancient philosophy presciently hailed as the common soul of nature"
   [[42]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#rom-schelling-1798-world-soul-universal-organism) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOcZDJDQgGkcePc8Lj.
10. **Fechner (1848–1861).** The question is now asked outright, as a list: "Sind die Pflanzen beseelt? Sind die
    Steine beseelt? Sind die Weltkörper beseelt? Ist die Welt beseelt?" [[43]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#soul-wo-fechner-1861-is-the-world-ensouled)
    https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgSckeOzyFru7JbNywO. The earth is "a living, more independent, more individually
    distinct being in a higher sense than we are ourselves" [[44]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#rom-fechner-1851-earth-more-alive-than-we)
    https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgOcWNrl434So9ln7JC. His sharpest line names the alternative to a world soul:
    "statt einer Weltseele giebt's eine Welt aus Seelenstaub" ("instead of a world soul, there is a world of
    soul-dust") [[45]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/romantic-naturphilosophie#soul-wo-fechner-1861-weltseele-or-soul-dust) https://sourcelibrary.org/q/BgSckeOzyFru7JbNyyC.
    *(SL's translator note glosses Weltseele as "collective spirit or life-force", which says more than the
    German; the claim quotes the German and is tagged `mistranslation`.)*

**Critique.** The living cosmos was never consensus. Lucretius denied it outright [[46]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-anc-living-world-was-contested).
The 1590–1620 "everything is alive" authors are not one world-soul school either: Campanella puts sense in each
thing's own form, "not … from the World Soul" [[47]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/renaissance#ren-campanella-sense-not-from-world-soul)
[[48]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/critique#crit-ren-panpsychism-not-one-world-soul).
